# [CS064] Layer Dependency Violation (arch-layer-violation)

A package imports a layer it may not depend on.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | LOW |
| **Category** | Architecture |
| **CWE** | - |
| **OWASP** | - |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

architecture.layers maps package patterns to layers and allowed_deps lists which layers each may import. A domain package importing a database adapter couples business rules to infrastructure and makes them hard to test.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
// internal/domain/order.go
import "example.com/app/internal/repository"
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
// internal/domain/order.go declares the interface it needs
type OrderStore interface {
	Save(ctx context.Context, o Order) error
}
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [arch-layer-violation]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    arch-layer-violation: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore arch-layer-violation -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** arch-layer-violation
```
